text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose the issue with your right ring finger, could you tell me when the swelling and pain started, and have you experienced any recent trauma or insect bites to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Can you describe the mechanism of injury in more detail, specifically did the finger get pulled straight or bent sideways? Also, are you experiencing any numbness or tingling in the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the mechanism of injury and your inability to flex the tip of the finger, I suspect a tendon injury. Can you confirm if you can actively bend the very last joint of your right ring finger, or does it remain straight when you try? Also, is there a palpable gap or defect at the tip of your finger?

The X-ray confirms no fracture, which strongly points to a soft tissue injury given your inability to flex the fingertip. This presentation is classic for a jersey finger, or avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon.
